audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer sides read 'Ekko' and the matchup was graded HARD 8/10, while the packet chart and all seven content win[] rows read Brand and the win rate is 50.15% over 329 games. The full-layer whys under those rows already argued that Brand wins them.
audit.why: Ekko's only ranged tool is Timewinder; his engage is a 325-range Phase Dive and a stun field that takes about three seconds to arm from 1600 range. Brand out-ranges and out-clears him through the laning phase; Ekko's threat is a snowballed skirmish, not a lane phase.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved to Brand, difficulty regraded TRICKY 7/10, Ekko's carry threat left at 8.5/10.

audit.why: The spikes array already lands the real timings: level 3-5 poke advantage, Chronobreak at 6, Liandry's punishing the W setup, and a snowballed Ekko flipping late skirmishes. The four suspectNames flagged by the packet ('Drive Resonance', 'Bait Parallel Convergence', 'Use Chronobreak', 'His Chronobreak') are false positives — every name matches the kit file.
audit.corrected: Left alone; only the hedge in whys[6] removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions were absent: Parallel Convergence shields Ekko when he enters his own anomaly, Phase Dive is an auto-attack reset, and Chronobreak makes him untargetable while healing him for damage taken.
audit.why: The shield changes the all-in maths, the auto reset means the wind-up rather than the cast is the cue to step back, and untargetability plus healing means the last chunk of damage you dump into a low Ekko can simply vanish — Grievous Wounds is the answer and the page never named it.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d and wants.you[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit, and dosFull[2].d called Chronobreak a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110/80/50 — never fifteen seconds. Parallel Convergence is 22s at rank 1 and Phase Dive 9s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into both fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and whys[6] hedged with 'generally'.
audit.why: Bullet bodies must match their titles, and a hedge says nothing.
audit.corrected: Both bullets replaced with title-matching kit facts; hedge removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Brand's W carries a derived 'terrain' flag.
audit.why: Riot's Pillar of Flame text is delayed area damage only; it does not create terrain or stop Phase Dive.
